rule: A landmark picks one of N clue scenes at random on each look, writes the picked index onto the viewer, and a later gate compares that stored index with its own fixed value by equality. Match opens the reward route; mismatch goes to a fixed fail place. Death sends the player to the same fail place with a second text state for the ghost.

data_fields.name: clue_pick
data_fields.unit: uniform random index on each look

data_fields.name: gate_rule
data_fields.unit: equality of stored key and door value

keep: One card per clue, shown at random on each look.
Stored last-look key on the character, not on the object.
Equality gate with one fixed value per door.
Fail place that is readable and not a hard death.
Second text state for a defeated or dead creature (alive long, dead short).
Two-voice sign: an authority title plus a rough second line from another hand.
One figure recurring across several doors, so the set reads as one story.
change: Their fail route is a teleport to a dark cell; ours should cost something legible (a 3-attacker fight at the door, or a lost turn).
Their clue reroll runs in the client (return_appearance); ours must roll on the server, seeded per character, zone and day, so a refresh cannot reroll.
Their murals are one-off prose; ours are catalogue fields per zone (700 zones as data) with a short card length cap.
Their trait tables are for chargen; ours would feed NPC one-line cards for the 100 Pit characters, not new names.
look_test: Build one wall with five door cards in one zone. Look, step back, look again: the clue card changes. Compare 1-line cards against 4-to-5-line cards on a 375-wide phone; time how long a card takes to read and pick a door. Judge whether a wrong door feels fair (a message, not a death). Second compare: the two-voice sign with and without the rough second line.
